evidence: Valid difference-eliminating argument backed by v_infraction. Variant A (shipped load-based) and variant B (SLA-target, ARIMA throughput loop + load loop) are two differently-designed control loops; both satisfy the planner's own window-mean TTFT/ITL control law yet both violate the tail SLA (TTFT p99 up to 3495ms; DB burst3 reactive achieved_p99=3494.7ms, is_violation=t, with reactive runs violating TTFT p99 across burst1/3/4/5 windows). Two independently-tuned loops failing identically eliminates loop tuning as the cause and localizes the defect to the shared mean-based capacity conversion (sizing so mean throughput meets mean demand leaves no room for the SLA-priced tail). The causal inference is warranted by the controlled comparison.
